thread:
camila: alert from monitoring — hosted API p95 timeouts and a spike in 5xx for tenant acct-834 within the last 3m :rotating_light:
camila: spike started around 2024-12-10T14:20:20Z, looks like queue depth climbed > 95% on several gateway hosts
infra-bot: [ALERT] hosted-gateway queue_util > 0.9 on gw-host-23, gw-host-24, gw-host-27
elaine: customer on slack reporting timeouts when sending multi-turn chat, getting 504s halfway through stream
ryan: seeing continuous-batch backlog increasing — pending_batches: 412 -> 890 in last 4m on region-us-west-1
sukh: any recent deploys?
ryan: no infra deploys in last 2h; model variants swapped earlier but that was low-traffic training jobs, unrelated
elaine: reproducer from customer (trimmed):
elaine: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-ACCT834
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model":"rwd-large-quant",
  "input":"long conversation repeated with ~1600 tokens prefix",
  "stream":true
}
```
elaine: they said error occurs after ~3-6s then stream closes with 504
camila: attached traces show requests queued on gateway for 2.8s before being dispatched, then worker returns timeout
ryan: logs from gw-host-23: ```
[14:21:02] accept request tenant=acct-834 seq=87 length=1580
[14:21:05] enqueue to continuous-batcher, queue_depth=98/100
[14:21:07] batcher-backlog=560, dequeue-latency=2250ms
[14:21:09] request timed out waiting for worker (timeout=2500ms) -> gateway 504
```
sukh: batcher config caps at queue_depth=100 by policy for region small hosts, once full we early-reject but looks like we were close to threshold and dequeue lag made things hit api timeout window
elaine: customer is on Hosted tier (not Dedicated) — they rely on our fallback routing. Why didn't requests route to a less-busy model variant?
ryan: routing policy should allow fallback to a cheaper/lower-latency variant if queue_depth > 0.9, but I see the route decision happened earlier and pinned to rwd-large-quant because their request included a pinned model param
camila: so pin prevents fallback — need to check canary fallback policy for pinned requests
sukh: immediate mitigations: 1) increase gateway request timeout to 5s for this tenant (quick patch) 2) temporarily raise queue_depth cap for affected hosts to 150 3) enable bypass batching for longseq requests from this tenant
ryan: plan: implement tenant-level throttling and prefer direct dispatch for >1200 token requests. Elaine can we ask customer to pass header `X-Prefer-Direct: 1` while we triage?
elaine: asked customer, they can add header for testing but need long-term fix from us
camila: debug checklist I've started:
- collect gw-host-23/24/27 batcher metrics (pending_batches, dequeue_time_hist) — in progress
- pull worker-side kvcache logs for seq handling — in progress
- verify routing rules for pinned models — assigned to ry an
ryan: got kvcache logs, KV warmups are triggering major stall when many longseqs request cold KV simultaneously. KVCACHE miss rate jumped to 78% for that tenant during the spike
elaine: could that explain dequeue latency?
sukh: yes, kvcache cold fills block the batcher worker threads briefly; with high concurrency that backpressure cascades into queueing and timeouts
camila: is this tenant doing a burst? traffic pattern shows 3x normal QPS between 14:18-14:26
elaine: customer confirmed a batch job kicked off new users hitting endpoints concurrently (unexpected ramp)
ryan: reproduced locally with a loadtest: 200 concurrent longseq requests, continuous-batcher backlog climbs and we start seeing gateway 504s in the same pattern
ryan: local reproduce script snippet:```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do \ 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -H "X-Prefer-Direct: 0" -X POST https://api.local/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-large-quant","input":"<1.5k tokens>","stream":true}' &
done
```
elaine: support-bot: created support ticket #SUP-1198 and escalated to priority-high for acct-834
support-bot: linked incident to runbook: "queue-depth-surge"
camila: short-term mitigation executed at 14:25: enable tenant throttle (rate-limit to 60 rps) + bumped queue_depth to 140 on gw-host-23/24 -> latency improved within 90s :thumbsup:
ryan: after bump p95 dropped to 320ms and 504s stopped for that tenant (monitoring graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/queue?orgId=1&from=1700000000000&to=1700000100000)
sukh: medium-term actions we agreed on:
- add heuristic: if request tokens > 1200, prefer direct dispatch path (skip continuous-batching)
- add tenant-aware kv-cache prewarm on sudden ramp (async warms for top n keys)
- avoid pinning fallback — honor fallback_when_queue_high even for pinned models if routing policy allows
- add circuit-breaker that opens when dequeue_time > 1500ms consistently for 30s
elaine: I've told customer we'll deploy mitigations and follow up in 4h with root cause
camila: infra note: need an RFC for changing default queue_depth caps for small hosts, plus a followup to add better telemetry for per-tenant kvcache miss spikes
ryan: I'll open a PR with the direct-dispatch toggle + unit tests
sukh: ops: add alert that correlates kvcache_miss_rate and batcher_dequeue_latency (right now alerts are separate)
elaine: customer asked for a runbook item for 'how to avoid 504 during tenant ramp' — I'll draft guidance: throttle client ramp, use X-Prefer-Direct for long sequences, avoid pinned models when you want fallback
camila: marking this incident P1 -> P2 after mitigations. Will keep thread open until PR merges and prewarm solution validated
ryan: quick note: don't increase global timeouts; that masks problems and increases user-perceived latency variance
elaine: thanks everyone, posting summary to the customer and closing after postmortem
infra-bot: [ACTION] created issue INFRA-4721: "tenant-aware kv prewarm + queue heuristic"
support-bot: [TICKET] SUP-1198 updated with incident notes and mitigation timeline
camila: ending notes: root cause = tenant-induced kvcache cold fills causing batcher worker stalls -> queue saturation -> gateway timeouts. Mitigations applied and PR in flight. :white_check_mark:
